metadata.title: Travel and Countries Reviewer Knowledge Pack
metadata.description: Full academy knowledge pack for travel, countries, borders, immigration, foreign references, and country commentary.

pack.title: Travel and Countries Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Provide reviewer knowledge for travel, country, border, migration, and foreign-reference reasoning without collapsing neutral observation into a finding.
protected_interests: review-only handling of ambiguous travel commentary
required_evidence: Travel mention | minimum: A literal reference to travel, movement, or a destination inside the chunk. | strong: A clearly described journey, route, or location sequence. | weak: A coded or abbreviated travel mention that still remains local to the text. | insufficient: An unrelated place name, a generic mention of movement, or a foreign reference without travel intent.

Border crossing | minimum: A literal border, customs, or entry mention. | strong: A passage showing departure, arrival, visa, or passport context. | weak: A short reference to crossing or entering that still needs context. | insufficient: A country mention without entry or border meaning.

Migration | minimum: A literal statement of immigration, emigration, exile, refugee status, or deportation. | strong: A scene that clearly describes forced movement or settlement. | weak: A short mention that implies migration but does not finish the thought. | insufficient: A neutral travel note or unrelated geography mention.

Country evaluation | minimum: A literal insult, praise, mockery, stereotype, or political attack aimed at a country or its people. | strong: A direct evaluative phrase that clearly treats the country as a target. | weak: A coded or joking line that still clearly carries the same evaluative meaning. | insufficient: A documentary, quote, or neutral comparison without abuse or endorsement.

Fictional travel | minimum: A literal dream, fantasy, fiction, or imaginary-country frame. | strong: A scene that clearly signals invented geography or non-real travel. | weak: A short imaginative marker that still needs surrounding context. | insufficient: A factual travel statement or a historical reference without fantasy framing.
insufficient_evidence: A neutral travel diary note with no evaluative language.
A documentary or news report repeating a travel phrase as evidence.
A quoted country insult that the story explicitly rejects.
A foreign place name used only as scenery or background.
reviewer_heuristics: Separate travel observation from evaluative country commentary.
Treat documentary, news, court, and police framing as factual unless the text clearly adds judgment.
Use historical framing to distinguish exile, migration, and remembrance from present-day attacks.
Treat fiction, dreams, flashbacks, and imaginary-country language as non-literal unless later text confirms reality.
Do not collapse country comparison into insult, praise, or propaganda unless the wording actually does so.
Travel dialogue, scene description, and narration may all be neutral and should not be forced into a finding.
Use review-only outcomes when the text is travel-related but the evaluative meaning is still ambiguous.
positive_examples: Direct country insult in dialogue: هذا البلد متخلف.
Direct travel mention with clear destination: الوجهة هي إسطنبول.
Historical migration line: في التاريخ القديم سافروا ثم استقروا هناك.
Fictional journey: في القصة سافر إلى بلد خيالي.
Country mockery in a debate scene: يا له من بلد مضحك.
Passport and visa planning: لا تنسَ الجواز والفيزا قبل السفر.
Country political critique with a clear target: النظام هناك فاسد.
Border crossing scene with explicit movement: عبرنا الحدود بعد الفجر.
negative_examples: Neutral travel diary: سافرنا إلى المدينة ثم عدنا مساءً.
Documentary reference: يشرح الفيلم مسار الهجرة القديمة بدون حكم.
Court transcript: يكرر الشاهد عبارة السفر كما قيلت في الملف.
Fictional frame: The story describes an imaginary country in a dream.
Educational geography lesson: يتحدث المعلم عن دول العالم بلا إهانة.
Travel planning only: الجواز جاهز والرحلة غداً.
Historical narration without endorsement: يروي المؤرخ قصة منفى قديم.
Border discussion without incitement: يتحدث الموظف عن إجراءات الدخول.
common_false_positives: Treating any mention of a country as a harmful finding.
Treating a neutral travel plan as a political or security statement.
Treating a dream, fantasy, or fiction frame as factual travel.
Treating a documentary or news report as endorsement.
Treating a country comparison as an insult or stereotype.
Treating a border or passport mention as migration harm without context.
Treating quoted country criticism as the narrator's own view.

glossary_relationships.note: Core travel anchor for factual or contextual travel mention.
Signals movement or destination when the text is about a trip.
Strong indicator of a travel scene or departure/arrival context.
Relevant when passport and entry context appear.
Relevant when the line discusses entry permission or travel authorisation.
Supports cross-border travel or entry reasoning.
Signals immigration, emigration, or displacement reasoning.
Supports refugee or forced movement reasoning.
Often historical or forced removal rather than ordinary travel.
Relevant for neutral foreign-country mentions and comparisons.
Relevant when the text compares or describes culture abroad.
Relevant when a foreign language is mentioned or learned.
Signals tourism and travel services reasoning.
Relevant when travel is fictional or dreamlike.

article_mapping.note: Use for factual travel mention, observation, or neutral country reference.
Use for historical travel, exile, migration, or remembered journeys.
Use for fictional, dreamlike, or imaginary travel contexts.
Use when the text clearly insults, praises, mocks, or stereotypes a country or its people.

reporting_guidance: Report the shortest exact phrase that carries the travel, migration, or country evaluation meaning.
Use reviewer comment language when the text is only travel observation, documentary description, or a neutral comparison.
Use a finding only when the wording clearly insults, praises, stereotypes, or politically attacks a country or its people.
Explain whether the text is factual, historical, fictional, dreamlike, quoted, or evaluative.
Mention review-only outcomes when the line is about travel but the country meaning is still ambiguous after context analysis.
